groups.definition_en: to separate a whole into parts, or to cut a continuity
groups.core_image: 整体被分开，或连续性被切断
groups.scene: 杯子摔在地上，你说 The glass cup broke into pieces.
groups.sceneCN: 这里 break 是「弄碎、打破」（第 1 个义项：物理断裂，分成碎片）；句意：那个玻璃杯摔成了碎片。

pos.zh: 打破；弄坏；违反（规则/承诺）

senses.title: Physical break: separate into pieces
senses.titleCN: 物理断裂：分成碎片（打破／弄碎）
senses.definition: to damage something by separating it into pieces
senses.definitionCN: 打破；弄碎；使某物裂成碎片
senses.example: Be careful not to break the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 小心别把玻璃杯打碎。
senses.why: The core sense: force separates one solid whole into parts.
senses.whyCN: 核心义：外力把一个固体整体分离成若干部分。

senses.title: Snap a bone or a branch
senses.definition: to crack or snap a bone, branch, or other long object
senses.definitionCN: 使（骨头、树枝等细长物体）折断
senses.example: He fell off his bike and broke his arm.
senses.exampleCN: 他从自行车上摔下来，摔断了胳膊。
senses.why: A bone or branch is a long whole; snapping it is still a physical split.
senses.whyCN: 骨头、树枝是细长的整体，折断它仍然属于物理上的分离。

senses.title: Break a rule, law, or promise
senses.definition: to fail to obey a rule, law, or promise
senses.definitionCN: 违反、违背（规则、法律、承诺）
senses.example: If you park here, you are breaking the law.
senses.exampleCN: 如果你把车停在这里，就是违法。
senses.why: A rule is a boundary; breaking it means cutting through that boundary. This is a common metaphorical extension.
senses.whyCN: 规则是一条边界，“打破”它就等于越过边界。这是一种常见的比喻性引申。

senses.title: Break the silence or a conversation
senses.titleCN: 打断：沉默、谈话或连续性
senses.definition: to interrupt something continuous, such as silence, a conversation, or a service
senses.definitionCN: 打断、中断（沉默、谈话、服务等连续的事物）
senses.example: A loud phone call broke the silence in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 一通响亮的电话打破了房间里的沉默。
senses.why: Silence and talk are continuous flows; a cut in the flow is a break.
senses.whyCN: 沉默和谈话都是连续的过程，在其中切一刀就是“打断”。

senses.title: Break down: a machine stops working
senses.titleCN: 坏掉：机器、设备停止工作
senses.definition: to stop working correctly, used about machines and equipment
senses.definitionCN: （机器、设备）坏掉、失灵
senses.example: My old laptop broke again, so I lost the file.
senses.exampleCN: 我的旧笔记本电脑又坏了，文件也丢了。
senses.why: A machine is a whole that works as a cycle; when the cycle fails, it is broken.
senses.whyCN: 机器是靠循环运转的整体，循环失效了就是“坏了”。

senses.title: Break a record or a limit
senses.definition: to do better than a previous record or limit
senses.definitionCN: 打破（纪录、上限）
senses.example: She broke the world record for the 100-metre race.
senses.exampleCN: 她打破了 100 米赛跑的世界纪录。
senses.why: A record is a ceiling or limit; passing it breaks the old boundary.
senses.whyCN: 纪录是一道天花板或上限，越过它就是“打破”旧边界。

senses.title: A break: rest, interval, or short holiday
senses.titleCN: 名词：休息、课间、短暂休假
senses.definition: a short period when you stop working, studying, or travelling
senses.definitionCN: （工作、学习、旅程中的）休息；课间；短暂休假
senses.example: Let's take a ten-minute break before we continue.
senses.exampleCN: 我们休息十分钟再继续吧。
senses.why: The noun keeps the image of a cut in continuity: a gap inside a longer stretch of work or time.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了“连续性被切开”的意象：一段较长的工作或时间中的一个缺口。

senses.title: A break: a chance or a lucky opening
senses.definition: a chance to do something, or a piece of good luck
senses.definitionCN: 机会；好运；（口语）喘息的机会
senses.example: That TV role was her big break.
senses.exampleCN: 那个电视角色是她人生的大好机会。
senses.why: A gap in a wall is an opening; a gap in bad luck is an opening for a chance. Give me a break can also mean stop pushing me.
senses.whyCN: 墙上的裂口是一个开口；厄运中的缺口就是机会的入口。give me a break 也可以表示“别逼我了”。

senses.title: Break up: a relationship ends
senses.definition: to end a relationship, or to make someone feel extremely sad
senses.definitionCN: （使关系）破裂；（使）心碎
senses.example: Their marriage broke up last year, and it broke her heart.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的婚姻去年破裂了，这让她心碎。
senses.why: A relationship is imagined as a whole; ending it splits that whole, and heartbreak is the emotional result.
senses.whyCN: 人们把关系想象成一个整体，结束关系就是把它分开，心碎是这一裂口带来的情感结果。

senses.title: Break a code
senses.definition: to find the meaning of a code or a secret message
senses.definitionCN: 破译（密码、暗号）
senses.example: The team finally broke the enemy's code.
senses.exampleCN: 团队最终破译了敌方的密码。
senses.why: A code is a closed, sealed whole; breaking it opens the surface and lets the meaning out. English also says crack a code.
senses.whyCN: 密码是一个封闭的整体，“打破”它就能打开表层、读出含义。英语里也常说 crack a code。

intro.en: The history of break runs from an old Germanic strong verb to a modern word family. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: break 的历史从一个古老的日耳曼语强动词，一路走到现代英语的词族。年代为大致估计。

items.en: brecan, a strong verb of class 4, meant 'to break, shatter, burst; to violate'. Its past forms bræc and brocen became modern broke and broken.
items.cn: 古英语 brecan 是第四类强动词，意为“打破、打碎、爆裂；违反”。它的过去式 bræc、过去分词 brocen 演变成今天的 broke、broken。

items.en: The ancestor is reconstructed as *brekaną, shared with German brechen and Dutch breken.
items.cn: 更早的祖词被重构为原始日耳曼语 *brekaną，德语 brechen、荷兰语 breken 都来自这一共同的词。

items.en: Most etymology handbooks trace it to a PIE root *bhrēg- (also written *bʰreg-), 'to break'. Reconstructed roots are not attested directly, and spellings differ between sources.
items.cn: 多数词源手册把它追溯到原始印欧语词根 *bhrēg-（也写作 *bʰreg-），意为“打破”。这类词根是重构出来的，并没有直接文献记录，不同资料的写法也可能不同。

items.en: Latin frangere 'to break' (past participle fractus) gave English fracture, fragment, fragile and fraction. Traditional teaching treats frag-/fract- as a separate family from Germanic break. Some historical sources do connect both to the same PIE root, so the safe wording is 'different borrowing paths, possible distant kinship'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 frangere“打破”（过去分词 fractus）产生了英语 fracture、fragment、fragile、fraction。传统教学把 frag-/fract- 看作与日耳曼语的 break 分开的词族；也有一些历史语言学资料把两者追溯到同一个印欧词根。所以更稳妥的说法是“不同借入路径，可能存在远亲关系”，而不是绝对“毫无关系”。

items.en: Modern English keeps the strong pattern break – broke – broken. The noun break, as in a rest or a chance, developed later from the verb.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了古老的强动词变化 break – broke – broken。表示休息或机会的名词 break，是后来从动词发展出来的。

note.en: Words below can be confused with break. The notes point to sound and spelling first, then meaning.
note.cn: 下面这些词容易和 break 混淆。说明先讲读音和拼写，再讲意思。

entries.definition: a device that slows or stops a vehicle; to use such a device. Same sound as break, different spelling and meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 刹车；用刹车减速。和 break 同音，但拼写和意思不同。

entries.definition: cold and empty; without hope. It adds an l and ends in /iːk/, not /eɪk/.
entries.definitionCN: 荒凉的；阴冷的；没有希望的。多了一个 l，结尾读 /iːk/，不是 /eɪk/。

entries.definition: food made from flour and baked. The ea is pronounced /e/, and the word ends in d, not k.
entries.definitionCN: 面包。ea 读 /e/，结尾是 d 而不是 k。

entries.definition: noun: baked food made from flour. break is a verb or noun about splitting; bread ends in -d and sounds like /bred/.
entries.definitionCN: 面包（名词）；break 是“打破／休息”，bread 以 d 结尾，读 /bred/。

entries.definition: noun: the chest, or a woman's milk-producing organ. It ends in -st after brea-, while break ends in -k.
entries.definitionCN: 胸部；乳房（名词）；breast 在 brea- 后面是 -st，而 break 是 -k。

entries.definition: noun: a hard block used for building. The vowel is short /ɪ/, and the word ends in ck.
entries.definitionCN: 砖块（名词）；元音是短音 /ɪ/，结尾是 ck。

entries.definition: adjective: cold, empty, and without hope. It has an extra l after b.
entries.definitionCN: 荒凉的；阴冷的；无望的（形容词）；b 后面多一个 l。

entries.definition: noun: the hard, pointed mouth of a bird. It is pronounced /biːk/, not /breɪk/.
entries.definitionCN: 鸟喙（名词）；读 /biːk/，不是 /breɪk/。

entries.definition: noun, verb or adjective: the top of a mountain or the highest point; to reach it. It is a homophone of beak, but starts with p.
entries.definitionCN: 山顶；最高点；达到顶峰（名词／动词／形容词）。它与 beak 同音，但开头是 p。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real, explainable links — compound words and common phrases, not made-up rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实、可解释的联系——复合词和常见短语，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: breakfast = break + fast. Here fast means going without food, not 'quick'. Breakfast is the meal that breaks the night's fast.
normal.cn: breakfast = break + fast。这里的 fast 是“禁食”，不是“快”。早餐就是打破夜间禁食的那一餐。

normal.en: break a record = break a ceiling. A record is an upper limit; breaking it means going above the old limit.
normal.cn: break a record = 打破天花板。纪录是一道上限，打破它就是从旧上限上面越过去。

normal.en: break someone's heart = split a whole. A heart is imagined as a whole; losing someone splits it, so the person is heartbroken.
normal.cn: break someone's heart = 把一个整体劈开。心被想象成一个整体，失去某人就像把它劈开，于是这个人“心碎”了。

normal.en: break the ice = break a barrier. Ice is a barrier between people; breaking it lets conversation start.
normal.cn: break the ice = 打破屏障。冰是人与人之间的屏障，打破它，谈话才能开始。

normal.en: give someone a break = open a gap. A break in pressure is an opening: stop pushing, or give the person a chance.
normal.cn: give someone a break = 打开一个缺口。压力中的“缺口”就是开口：别再逼他，或者给他一个机会。

abstract.en: Abstractly, break is an operation on wholeness: apply force, draw a line of separation, and where there was one continuous thing there are now two parts — or a gap.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，break 是对“整体”做的一次操作：施加力，画出一条分离线，原本一个连续的东西就变成两个部分——或者留下一个缺口。

abstract.en: The extended senses keep this geometry: a limit is a line to cross, a flow is a line to cut, a working system is a loop that stops, and a secret is a sealed surface that opens.
abstract.cn: 各个引申义都保留了这个几何形状：上限是一条要越过的线，连续的过程是一条要被切开的线，运转的系统是一个会停下的循环，秘密是一个会被打开的封闭表面。

abstract.en: So break does not change meaning randomly. It takes one shape — separation — and moves it from objects to rules, time, machines, relationships and information.
abstract.cn: 所以 break 的词义并不是随便变化的：它把“分离”这一个形状，从物体搬到规则、时间、机器、关系和信息上。

examples.en: Be careful not to break the glass vase.
examples.cn: 小心别打碎那个玻璃花瓶。

examples.en: Let's take a break after finishing the work.
examples.cn: 做完工作后我们休息一下吧。

examples.en: The car broke down on the highway.
examples.cn: 汽车在高速公路上抛锚了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 不锐刻（break）—— 要是不用锐器刻划它，它就不会破裂 → break

groups.root: 源自古英语 brecan，核心含义为“分裂、断裂”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten common senses of break. Each grows from one core image: a whole is split, or a continuity is cut.
sensesIntro.cn: break 的十个常见义项。每一个都从同一个核心意象长出来：整体被分开，或者连续性被切断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one whole → force → split → two parts / a gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个整体 → 施加力 → 裂开 → 两个部分／一个缺口。

branches.en: PHYSICAL SPLIT: force separates a solid whole — glass, bone, branch.
branches.cn: 物理分离：外力让固体整体裂开——玻璃、骨头、树枝。

branches.en: BOUNDARY BROKEN: rules, limits and records act as boundaries; crossing them breaks them.
branches.cn: 边界被突破：规则、上限、纪录都是边界，越过它们就是“打破”。

branches.en: CONTINUITY CUT: silence, talk, work and time are flows; a gap cut into them is an interruption or a rest.
branches.cn: 连续性中断：沉默、谈话、工作、时间都是连续流，在其中切出缺口就是打断或休息。

branches.en: FUNCTION STOPPED: a machine is a working whole; when its working order fails, it is broken.
branches.cn: 功能停止：机器是运转的整体，运转秩序失效就是“坏了”。

branches.en: OPENING IN A WHOLE: a gap can be a chance, a split can end a bond, and a sealed code can be opened.
branches.cn: 整体上的开口：缺口可以成为机会，裂口可以结束关系，封闭的密码可以被打开。

intro.en: break is a productive root: prefixes and suffixes aim its core idea of splitting or interrupting at new meanings.
intro.cn: break 是一个能产的词根：前缀和后缀把它“分开／中断”的核心意思引导到新的含义上。

latinIntro.en: English also borrowed a second 'breaking' family from Latin frangere 'to break' (past participle fractus). Its English forms use frag-, fract- or frac-.
latinIntro.cn: 英语还从拉丁语 frangere“打破”（过去分词 fractus）借来第二个“断裂”词族，在英语中写作 frag-、fract- 或 frac-。

items.meaning: able to be broken
items.meaningCN: 可被打碎的（-able 是形容词后缀，表示“能被……的”）
items.example: These glasses are breakable, so wash them carefully.
items.exampleCN: 这些玻璃杯容易碎，清洗时要小心。

items.meaning: impossible to break
items.meaningCN: 打不碎的；牢不可破的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: This phone case is almost unbreakable.
items.exampleCN: 这个手机壳几乎摔不坏。

items.meaning: damage caused by breaking; the amount of things broken
items.meaningCN: 破损；破损量（-age 是名词后缀，表示行为、结果或总量）
items.example: The shop adds a small charge to cover breakage.
items.exampleCN: 这家店会加收一点费用来弥补破损损失。

items.meaning: a sudden start of a disease, war, or violence
items.meaningCN: 爆发（疾病、战争、暴力等）（out- 表示“向外、突然出现”）
items.example: An outbreak of flu closed the school for a week.
items.exampleCN: 一场流感爆发让学校停课一周。

items.meaning: a failure of a machine or system; also a detailed analysis
items.meaningCN: 故障；崩溃；（问题、信息的）细分、分析（down 表示“向下、彻底”）
items.example: My car had a breakdown on the motorway.
items.exampleCN: 我的车在高速公路上抛锚了。

items.meaning: a group or player that separates from a larger group; a sudden attack in sport
items.meaningCN: 脱离群体的一派；体育比赛中的快速反击（away 表示“离开、分开”）
items.example: A breakaway group of members formed a new club.
items.exampleCN: 一批脱离原组织的成员成立了新俱乐部。

items.meaning: very great sadness, especially caused by love
items.meaningCN: 心碎；极度悲伤（尤指因爱情）
items.example: The song is about love and heartbreak.
items.exampleCN: 这首歌讲的是爱情与心碎。

items.meaning: the first meal of the day, which breaks the night's fast
items.meaningCN: 早餐（break 打破 + fast 禁食，即“打破夜间的禁食”）
items.example: I usually have eggs and toast for breakfast.
items.exampleCN: 我早餐通常吃鸡蛋和吐司。

items.meaning: a wall built in the sea to break the force of waves
items.meaningCN: 防波堤（用来打散海浪力量的海中墙体）
items.example: The breakwater keeps the harbour calm.
items.exampleCN: 防波堤让港口保持平静。

items.meaning: an important discovery or advance that gets past an old limit
items.meaningCN: 突破；重大进展（through 表示“穿过”，越过旧界限）
items.example: The team made a breakthrough in battery research.
items.exampleCN: 团队在电池研究上取得了突破。

items.meaning: something that breaks; a circuit breaker cuts off electric current
items.meaningCN: 破坏者；断路器（-er 表示做动作的人或物）
items.example: A circuit breaker cuts the power when there is a fault.
items.exampleCN: 出现故障时，断路器会切断电源。

latinEntries.meaning: a crack or break, especially in a bone; also a verb meaning to break
latinEntries.meaningCN: 骨折；断裂（也可作动词：使断裂）

latinEntries.meaning: a small piece broken off something
easily broken or damaged
a part of a whole; a small piece

groups.definition_en: to come to have something, or to reach a new state
groups.core_image: 从没有到有，或变成另一种状态
groups.scene: 天黑后才到家，你说 We got home after dark.
groups.sceneCN: 这里 get 是「到达」（第 4 个义项：走完路径到达终点）；句意：我们天黑之后才到家。

pos.zh: 变得（get + 形容词／过去分词，表示进入某状态）

derivatives.zh: 进取心强、主动争取的人

senses.title: Obtain: come to have
senses.titleCN: 得到：把东西拿到自己手里
senses.definition: to obtain or come to have something
senses.definitionCN: 得到；获得（某物）
senses.example: I got a new bike for my birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 我生日得到了一辆新自行车。
senses.why: Get starts with a source outside you. You move toward it, reach it, and it becomes yours: the path ends in possession.
senses.whyCN: get 的起点是你之外的源头：你朝它移动、够到它，它才归你所有——路径的终点就是“拥有”。

senses.title: Receive: something comes to you
senses.titleCN: 收到：东西从外面来到你这里
senses.definition: to receive something that is sent or given to you
senses.definitionCN: 收到；接到（寄来或给予的东西）
senses.example: Did you get my message?
senses.exampleCN: 你收到我的消息了吗？
senses.why: Here the path runs the other way: the thing travels to you instead of you travelling to it. The result is the same — it is now in your hands.
senses.whyCN: 这里路径方向相反：不是你走向它，而是它来到你这里；结果相同——它现在在你手里。

senses.title: Fetch: go and bring something back
senses.titleCN: 去取来：走到源头再带回来
senses.definition: to go to a place and bring something back
senses.definitionCN: 去取；去拿回来
senses.example: Can you get me a glass of water?
senses.exampleCN: 你能给我拿一杯水来吗？
senses.why: This is the full geometry of get: leave your place, go to the source, take, and return. The word covers the whole round trip, not just the grabbing.
senses.whyCN: 这是 get 的完整路径：离开原地、走到源头、拿取、再回来。这个词覆盖整个往返过程，而不只是“抓”的动作。

senses.title: Reach: arrive at a place
senses.titleCN: 到达：走完路径到达终点
senses.definition: to arrive at a place or reach a point
senses.definitionCN: 到达；抵达（某地或某一点）
senses.example: How do I get to the station?
senses.exampleCN: 去车站怎么走？
senses.why: If getting something means moving along a path until you have it, then getting somewhere is the same path with a place as its end point. Arrival is possession of a location.
senses.whyCN: 如果“得到东西”是沿路径走到拥有它，那么“到达某地”就是同一路径把地点当作终点。抵达就是“拥有一个位置”。

senses.title: Become: pass into a new state
senses.definition: to become or start to be in a particular state
senses.definitionCN: 变得；开始处于某种状态
senses.example: It's getting dark, so let's go home.
senses.exampleCN: 天快黑了，我们回家吧。
senses.why: Possession can be abstract: you 'get' a state in the same way you get an object. The path now ends not in a thing but in a condition — dark, tired, ready.
senses.whyCN: “拥有”可以是抽象的：你像得到一个物件那样“得到”一种状态。路径的终点不再是东西，而是某种状况——黑、累、准备好。

senses.title: Cause: make something happen
senses.titleCN: 使役：让别人或别物进入某状态
senses.definition: to cause someone or something to do something or be in a state
senses.definitionCN: 让……做；使……变成
senses.example: I finally got him to agree.
senses.exampleCN: 我终于让他同意了。
senses.why: If a person can get a state, that person can also get another person into a state. The same 'bring to an end point' now works through a causal link.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个人能得到一种状态，他也能把另一个人“弄到”某种状态。同一个“带到终点”的动作，现在通过因果关系施加出去。

senses.title: Understand: grasp with the mind
senses.definition: to understand something, especially a joke or an idea
senses.definitionCN: 理解；明白（笑话、想法）
senses.example: Sorry, I don't get the joke.
senses.exampleCN: 抱歉，我没听懂这个笑话。
senses.why: Understanding is physical grasping moved inward: the mind reaches out, takes the idea, and holds it. English uses grasp and catch in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 理解是把“抓住”从手上搬到脑子里：心智伸出去、拿住想法。英语里 grasp、catch 也是同样的用法。

senses.title: Catch an illness
senses.definition: to become ill with a disease
senses.definitionCN: 得（病）；染上（疾病）
senses.example: I got a cold from my roommate.
senses.exampleCN: 我被室友传染了感冒。
senses.why: An illness is something unwanted that comes to you and then stays with you. It follows the receive path, but the thing received is a condition.
senses.whyCN: 疾病是一种不请自来、来了就留在你身上的东西。它走的是“收到”的路径，只是收到的是疾病这种状态。

senses.title: Get + past participle: change of state
senses.titleCN: get + 过去分词：进入新状态
senses.definition: used with a past participle to show that someone or something enters a new state
senses.definitionCN: 与过去分词连用，表示进入某种新状态（如结婚、迷路、穿好）
senses.example: They got married last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们去年春天结婚了。
senses.why: This is become in grammar form: get supplies the movement, the participle supplies the end state. The phrase profiles the change, not the state itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是“变得”的语法形式：get 提供“移动”，过去分词提供终点状态。这个结构强调变化过程，而不是状态本身。

senses.title: Have got: possession in speech
senses.definition: used in informal British English to mean 'have' or 'must'
senses.definitionCN: （英式口语）有；必须
senses.example: I've got two tickets for tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 我有两张今晚的票。
senses.why: Have got began as 'have obtained': the result of getting is still in your hands, so the perfect form came to mean plain possession.
senses.whyCN: have got 原本是“已经得到”：得到的结果还在手里，于是完成形式逐渐表示单纯的“拥有”。

intro.en: Get came into Middle English from Old Norse, while native Old English kept the same root mostly inside compounds. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: get 在中古英语时期从古诺斯语进入英语；本土古英语主要把这个词根保留在复合词里。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Middle English geten came from Old Norse geta 'to obtain, reach; to be able; to beget; to learn', a verb of very wide meaning (past tense gatum, past participle getenn).
items.cn: 中古英语 geten 来自古诺斯语 geta，意为“获得、到达；能够；生育；学会”，是一个含义非常宽的动词（过去式 gatum，过去分词 getenn）。

items.en: Old English had the same root mainly in compounds such as begietan 'to get, beget' and forgietan 'to forget'. The old past tense gat survives in biblical begat, and the old participle survives in gotten.
items.cn: 古英语主要把这个词根用在复合词里，如 begietan“取得、生育”和 forgietan“忘记”。古老的过去式 gat 还留在《圣经》式的 begat 里，古老的过去分词则留在 gotten 里。

items.en: The ancestor is reconstructed as *getan, also the source of Old Swedish gissa 'to guess' (literally 'to try to get') and Gothic bigitan 'to find'. German vergessen 'to forget' belongs to the same compound family.
items.cn: 更早的祖词被重构为原始日耳曼语 *getan，它也是古瑞典语 gissa“猜”（字面义“试着得到”）和哥特语 bigitan“找到”的来源。德语 vergessen“忘记”属于同一个复合词族。

items.en: Standard references trace it to PIE *ghend- (also written *ghed-), 'to seize, take'. Latin prehendere 'to seize' comes from the same root, which is why apprehend and comprehend belong here.
items.cn: 通行词源资料把它追溯到原始印欧语词根 *ghend-（也写作 *ghed-），意为“抓住、拿取”。拉丁语 prehendere“抓住”同出这一词根，所以 apprehend、comprehend 也属于这一族。

items.en: Modern English keeps got as the past tense. The past participle is got in British English and usually gotten in American English. The phrase have got developed from 'have obtained' into a plain marker of possession.
items.cn: 现代英语用 got 作过去式。过去分词在英式英语中多用 got，在美式英语中通常用 gotten。短语 have got 从“已经得到”发展成了单纯的“拥有”标记。

note.en: Words below can be confused with get. The notes point to sound and spelling first, then meaning.
note.cn: 下面这些词容易和 get 混淆。说明先讲读音和拼写，再讲意思。

entries.definition: a door or opening in a wall or fence. The vowel is /eɪ/, not /e/, and it ends in -te.
entries.definitionCN: 大门；围墙或栅栏上的开口。元音是 /eɪ/，不是 /e/，结尾是 -te。

entries.definition: the intestines; also a verb meaning to remove the inside of something. The vowel is /ʌ/, not /e/.
entries.definitionCN: 肠子；也可作动词，表示“取出内部东西”。元音是 /ʌ/，不是 /e/。

entries.definition: to give an answer without being sure. It has the same vowel but ends in -ss, not -t.
entries.definitionCN: 猜；在不确定时给出答案。元音相同，但结尾是 -ss，不是 -t。

entries.definition: the past tense of get (British /ɡɒt/, American /ɡɑːt/). It is not a different word, just a different form.
entries.definitionCN: get 的过去式（英式 /ɡɒt/，美式 /ɡɑːt/）。它不是另一个词，只是同一个词的不同形式。

entries.definition: past tense of get. get is the present form; got has o instead of e and marks past time.
entries.definitionCN: get 的过去式。get 是现在形式；got 把 e 换成 o，并表示过去。

entries.definition: the American past participle of get. It adds a double t and -en, so it looks longer than got.
entries.definitionCN: get 的美式过去分词。它多了双 t 和 -en，看起来比 got 长。

entries.definition: the main point or general meaning of something. It looks like get plus -st, but starts with /dʒ/, not /ɡ/.
entries.definitionCN: 要点；大意。它看起来像 get 加 -st，但开头读 /dʒ/，不是 /ɡ/。

entries.definition: a door in a wall or fence. It looks like g + ate; the vowel letter is the same, but the sound is different.
entries.definitionCN: 大门；围墙或栅栏上的门。它看起来像 g + ate；元音字母相同，但读音不同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real, explainable links — real prefixes, compounds and common phrases, not made-up rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实、可解释的联系——真实的前缀、复合词和常见短语，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: forget = for- (away, off) + get. To 'un-get' something from the mind is to lose the ability to recall it.
normal.cn: forget = for-（离开、去掉）+ get。把某物从脑子里“去掉”，就是失去回忆它的能力，也就是忘记。

normal.en: beget = be- (an old verb prefix, here with a causative force) + get. To beget a child is to 'get' a new person into being.
normal.cn: beget = be-（古英语动词前缀，这里带使役意味）+ get。beget a child 就是让一个新生命“产生出来”。

normal.en: get-together = get + together. When people get together, the result is a get-together.
normal.cn: get-together = get + together。人们 get together（聚到一起），结果就是一场 get-together（聚会）。

normal.en: getaway = get + away. A getaway is the act of getting away, or a short trip away from work.
normal.cn: getaway = get + away。getaway 就是“离开”这个动作，或者离开工作的一趟短假。

normal.en: have got = have obtained. The perfect form still shows the result: what you got is in your hands, so 'I've got it' means 'I have it'.
normal.cn: have got = 已经得到。完成形式仍保留结果：你得到的东西还在手里，所以 I've got it 就是“我有它”。

abstract.en: Abstractly, get is a movement that ends in contact: an empty hand leaves, travels, closes, and comes back full. Symbol: ○ →→ ●.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，get 是一段以“接触”结束的移动：空手出发、经过路径、合拢、然后满载而归。符号：○ →→ ●。

abstract.en: The same arrow can point at an object (obtain), at a place (arrive), at a state (become), or at an idea (understand). In every case something is reached and held.
abstract.cn: 同一个箭头可以指向物件（得到）、指向地点（到达）、指向状态（变得）或指向想法（理解）。无论指向什么，都是“够到并握住”。

abstract.en: So get is one geometry — approach until contact — applied to objects, places, conditions and thoughts. It never means 'stay'; it always means 'come to be at'.
abstract.cn: 所以 get 是一个几何动作——一直靠近，直到接触——再把它施加到物件、地点、状况和想法上。它从不表示“停留”，而总是表示“来到某个位置／状态”。

examples.en: I got a letter from my sister yesterday.
examples.cn: 我昨天收到了姐姐的一封信。

examples.en: It's getting cold outside, so wear a coat.
examples.cn: 外面越来越冷了，穿件外套吧。

examples.en: She got the job after two interviews.
examples.cn: 两轮面试后，她得到了这份工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 盖特（get）—— 把奖品盖在手底下，它就归你了 → get 得到

groups.root: 源自古诺斯语 geta，核心含义为“取得、抓住”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten common senses of get. They follow one path: start outside, move toward, reach, hold — then let the held thing become a place or a state.
sensesIntro.cn: get 的十个常见义项。它们沿着同一条路径：从外面出发、朝目标移动、够到、握住——再让“握住的东西”变成一个地点或一种状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: from nothing → path → contact → in hand → new state.
core.cn: 核心意象：从无 → 路径 → 接触 → 到手 → 新状态。

branches.en: TWO DIRECTIONS: you go to the source (obtain), or the source comes to you (receive).
branches.cn: 两个方向：你走向源头（得到），或者源头走向你（收到）。

branches.en: PATH AND END POINT: fetch is a round trip to the source and back; arrive is a one-way trip to a place.
branches.cn: 路径与终点：fetch（去取来）是走到源头再回来的往返；arrive（到达）是走到某个地点的一次单程。

branches.en: STATE AS POSSESSION: become, get + past participle, and have got all treat a state like something held.
branches.cn: 状态即拥有：become、get + 过去分词、have got 都把一种状态当作“握在手里的东西”。

branches.en: CAUSATION: make someone else reach a state, as if bringing them to an end point.
branches.cn: 使役：让别人抵达某种状态，就像把别人带到终点。

branches.en: INWARD AND UNWANTED: grasp an idea in the mind; receive an illness in the body.
branches.cn: 向内与不请自来：在脑子里抓住一个想法；在身体上接收一种疾病。

intro.en: Get is a productive verb root: prefixes and suffixes aim its core idea of reaching and holding at new meanings.
intro.cn: get 是一个能产的动词词根：前缀和后缀把它“够到并握住”的核心意思引导到新的含义上。

latinIntro.en: English also borrowed a cognate family from Latin prehendere 'to seize' (past participle prehensus). It appears in English as prehend- or prehens-. Both families go back to PIE *ghend-.
latinIntro.cn: 英语还从拉丁语 prehendere“抓住”（过去分词 prehensus）借来一个同源词族，在英语中写作 prehend- 或 prehens-。这两个词族都追溯到原始印欧语 *ghend-。

items.meaning: to fail to remember; literally to 'un-get' something from the mind
items.meaningCN: 忘记（for- 表示“离开、去掉”，字面义是“把某物从脑子里去掉”）
items.example: I forgot his name again.
items.exampleCN: 我又忘了他的名字。

items.meaning: to bring a child into being; to cause something
items.meaningCN: 生育；引起（be- 是古英语动词前缀，含“围绕、加强”义）
items.example: Violence begets violence.
items.exampleCN: 暴力会滋生暴力。

items.meaning: a person who gets; also a material that absorbs residual gas inside a vacuum tube
items.meaningCN: 获得者；吸气剂（真空管中吸收残余气体的材料）（-er 表示做动作的人或物）
items.example: A getter removes leftover gas from the tube.
items.exampleCN: 吸气剂会清除管中残余的气体。

items.meaning: an escape, especially by a criminal; also a short holiday
items.meaningCN: 逃跑（尤指作案后）；短假（away 表示“离开”）
items.example: The thieves made a quick getaway.
items.exampleCN: 窃贼迅速逃走了。

items.meaning: an informal meeting or party
items.meaningCN: 非正式聚会（together 表示“聚到一起”）
items.example: We're having a small get-together on Friday.
items.exampleCN: 我们周五有个小型聚会。

items.meaning: an outfit, especially an unusual one
items.meaningCN: （口语）装束、打扮（尤指奇特的穿着）
items.example: He arrived in a strange getup.
items.exampleCN: 他穿着一身奇怪的装束来了。

items.meaning: impossible to forget
items.meaningCN: 难以忘怀的（un- 表示否定，-able 表示“能被……的”）
items.example: It was an unforgettable trip.
items.exampleCN: 那是一次难忘的旅行。

items.meaning: often forgetting things
items.meaningCN: 健忘的（-ful 表示“充满……的”）
items.example: My grandfather has become forgetful.
items.exampleCN: 我爷爷变得健忘了。

latinEntries.meaning: to seize or arrest; to understand
latinEntries.meaningCN: 逮捕；理解（抓住某人，或在心里抓住某个意思）

latinEntries.meaning: to grasp mentally; to include
latinEntries.meaningCN: 理解；包含（把意思整体抓住）

latinEntries.meaning: covering everything; complete
latinEntries.meaningCN: 全面的；综合的（把所有部分都抓住）

latinEntries.meaning: able to grasp, as a monkey's tail
latinEntries.meaningCN: 能抓握的（如猴子的尾巴）（-ile 表示“能……的”）

groups.definition_en: brightness that makes things visible; not heavy in weight
groups.core_image: 让黑暗或重量没有负担
groups.scene: 拎起朋友的包说 Wow, this is light!
groups.sceneCN: 这里 light 是「轻的」（第 5 个义项：重量小）；句意：哇，这个（包）好轻！

pos.zh: 轻的；浅色的；轻微的；轻松的

collocations.zh: 点亮；照亮；（脸上）露出喜色

forms.label: 比较级（形容词“轻的／浅的”）
最高级（形容词“轻的／浅的”）

derivatives.zh: 打火机（也可作形容词 light 的比较级）

senses.title: Light: brightness that lets you see
senses.definition: the natural energy from the sun, or brightness from a lamp, that makes things visible
senses.definitionCN: 光；光线；日光
senses.example: The light in this room is too bright.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间的光太亮了。
senses.why: Core sense: light removes darkness, and with darkness removed, things become visible. Every other sense of 'light' starts from this visible-energy image.
senses.whyCN: 核心义：光让黑暗消失，黑暗消失后事物就可见。light 的其他含义都从这个“可见的能量”意象出发。

senses.title: A light: a lamp or a source of light
senses.definition: a device or a source that produces light, such as a lamp
senses.definitionCN: 灯；光源
senses.example: Please turn on the light.
senses.exampleCN: 请把灯打开。
senses.why: Metonymy: the thing that carries the brightness is called by the brightness itself. The source stands for the light it gives.
senses.whyCN: 转喻：承载光亮的东西直接用“光”来称呼。光源代替了它所发出的光。

senses.title: Light: set something burning
senses.definition: to make something start to burn
senses.definitionCN: 点燃；点着
senses.example: She lit a candle and sat down.
senses.exampleCN: 她点了一支蜡烛，然后坐下。
senses.why: Fire is a source of light. To make fire start is to bring that light into existence, so the verb light means 'cause to give light by burning'.
senses.whyCN: 火是光的来源。让火开始，就是让那种光出现，所以动词 light 表示“使燃烧而发光”。

senses.title: Light: give light to a place
senses.definition: to give light to a place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 照亮；为……提供光
senses.example: The whole street was lit by the setting sun.
senses.exampleCN: 整条街道被夕阳照亮。
senses.why: The same light-energy is now directed onto an object. The object moves from dark to visible, which is the core change.
senses.whyCN: 同一种光能被导向某个对象；对象从暗变亮，这正是核心变化。

senses.title: Light: not heavy
senses.definition: not heavy; weighing little
senses.definitionCN: 轻的；不重的
senses.example: This bag is light enough to carry all day.
senses.exampleCN: 这个包很轻，可以整天提着。
senses.why: This is a different word that happens to share the spelling. Its own core is 'little weight', so a light load is a load that does not press on you.
senses.whyCN: 这是另一个恰好同形的词。它自己的核心是“重量小”，所以 light 的负担是不会压着你的负担。

senses.title: Light: pale in colour
senses.definition: pale in colour; not dark
senses.definitionCN: 浅色的；淡的
senses.example: She painted the walls light blue.
senses.exampleCN: 她把墙刷成了浅蓝色。
senses.why: Colour is judged by how much light it seems to hold. A pale colour looks 'full of light', so light came to mean the opposite of dark in colour too.
senses.whyCN: 人们用“含光量”来判断颜色：浅色看起来“充满光”，于是 light 也从“光线充足”引申为颜色上的“淡”。

senses.title: Light: not great in amount or force
senses.definition: not great in amount, force, or severity
senses.definitionCN: 轻微的；少量的；不严重的
senses.example: A light rain began to fall.
senses.exampleCN: 开始下起了小雨。
senses.why: From 'little weight' comes 'little force': a light rain, a light touch, a light punishment all carry little weight or pressure.
senses.whyCN: 从“重量小”引申出“力度小”：小雨、轻触、轻罚，都是分量或压力很小的东西。

senses.title: Light: not serious or difficult
senses.definition: not serious, difficult, or heavy in tone
senses.definitionCN: 轻松的；不严肃的；供消遣的
senses.example: We watched a light comedy after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后我们看了一部轻松喜剧。
senses.why: Something without weight is easy to carry. A task or a story without 'weight' is easy to bear, so light means entertaining and not serious.
senses.whyCN: 没有重量的东西容易拿；没有“分量”的任务或故事也容易承受，于是 light 表示轻松、不严肃。

senses.title: Come to light: become known
senses.titleCN: 显露：被人看见、为人所知
senses.definition: to become known or visible, especially after being hidden
senses.definitionCN: （come to light）被发现；显露出来
senses.example: New facts came to light during the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 审判过程中新的证据被披露出来。
senses.why: Hidden things are in darkness; when they come into the light, they become visible. Knowledge is treated as sight.
senses.whyCN: 隐藏的事物处在黑暗里；一旦进入光中，就变得可见。知识被当作“看见”。

senses.title: In a new light: from a different view
senses.definition: a particular way of considering something
senses.definitionCN: （in a new/different light）从新的角度；以不同的眼光
senses.example: The letter made her see his decision in a new light.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信让她从新的角度看待他的决定。
senses.why: Lighting determines what you can see and how it looks. A different light on an object is a different view of it.
senses.whyCN: 光线决定你能看见什么、它看起来怎样。换一束光照同一个对象，就是换一个视角看它。

intro.en: The spelling light hides two different words: one from 'bright', one from 'not heavy'. Both were lēoht in Old English and fell together in Modern English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: light 这个拼写下藏着两个不同的词：一个来自“明亮”，一个来自“不重”。它们在古英语里都写作 lēoht，在现代英语中合成了一个同形词。年代为大致估计。

items.en: lēoht (West Saxon), lēht (Anglian) meant 'light, daylight; bright, shining', as both noun and adjective. The -gh- spelling was later added by Anglo-French scribes to show the Germanic h-sound.
items.cn: lēoht（西撒克逊）、lēht（盎格利亚）意为“光、日光；明亮的、发光的”，既是名词也是形容词。后来的 -gh- 拼法是盎格鲁-法语抄写员为了标出日耳曼语的 h 音而加的。

items.en: From Proto-Germanic *leuhtą / *leuhta- (German Licht, Dutch licht, Gothic liuhaþ), from PIE *leuk- 'light, brightness'. Latin lux, lūcis 'light' and lūmen 'light' come from the same root, as does Greek leukos 'white'.
items.cn: 来自原始日耳曼语 *leuhtą / *leuhta-（德语 Licht、荷兰语 licht、哥特语 liuhaþ），再往前是原始印欧语 *leuk-“光、明亮”。拉丁语 lux、lūcis“光”和 lūmen“光”同出这一词根，希腊语 leukos“白”也是。

items.en: A separate lēoht meant 'not heavy, lightly built; easy, slight, quick'. It comes from Proto-Germanic *lingkhtaz (Old Norse léttr, German leicht, Dutch licht, Gothic leihts), from PIE *legwh- 'not heavy'.
items.cn: 另一个 lēoht 意为“不重、结构轻巧；容易的、轻微的、敏捷的”。它来自原始日耳曼语 *lingkhtaz（古诺斯语 léttr、德语 leicht、荷兰语 licht、哥特语 leihts），再往前是原始印欧语 *legwh-“不重”。

items.en: Standard etymological dictionaries treat the 'bright' light and the 'not heavy' light as different words from different roots. A few older popular accounts try to connect them through 'bright, clear → easy', but that link is not generally accepted.
items.cn: 标准词源词典把“明亮”的 light 和“不重”的 light 看作来自不同词根的两个词。少数较早的通俗说法试图用“明亮、清楚 → 容易”把两者连起来，但这一联系并未被普遍接受。

items.en: Latin lux / lūcis and lūmen gave English lucid, translucent, luminous and illuminate. Greek leukos 'white' gave leukemia and leukocyte. These are cognates of the 'brightness' light through PIE *leuk-, not borrowings of the English word.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lux / lūcis 和 lūmen 产生了英语 lucid、translucent、luminous、illuminate。希腊语 leukos“白”产生了 leukemia、leukocyte。它们通过原始印欧语 *leuk- 与“明亮”义的 light 同源，并不是直接借用了英语这个词。

items.en: The verb has two paths: light 'ignite / illuminate' comes from Old English līhtan (from the noun), while light 'alight, get down' comes from līhtan 'make light, relieve of weight' — a rare crossing between the two families. The past tense is lit, with lighted kept in attributive and compound uses.
items.cn: 动词有两条来路：表示“点燃／照亮”的 light 来自古英语 līhtan（源自名词）；表示“下车、下来”的 light 来自 līhtan“使变轻、卸下重量”——这是两个词族少见的交叉。过去式常用 lit，lighted 多保留在定语和复合词中。

note.en: Words below can be confused with light. The notes point to sound and spelling first, then meaning.
note.cn: 下面这些词容易和 light 混淆。说明先讲读音和拼写，再讲意思。

entries.definition: an informal or advertising spelling of light, used for low-calorie or low-fat products. It works as an adjective, not as a verb or a lamp.
entries.definitionCN: light 的非正式／广告拼法，常用于低热量、低脂产品。它只作形容词，不作动词或“灯”。

entries.definition: a verb meaning to get off a bus, train, or other vehicle; also an adjective meaning 'burning'. The extra a- changes both form and meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，表示从公共汽车、火车等下来；也可作形容词，表示“燃烧着的”。多出的 a- 让形式和意思都变了。

entries.definition: great pleasure; to please someone greatly. It begins with de-, not with l-, so it is not a form of light.
entries.definitionCN: 高兴；使某人非常愉快。它以 de- 开头，不是 l- 开头，所以不是 light 的某种形式。

entries.definition: adjective: small in degree; verb: to treat someone without respect. It adds s- before light.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：轻微的、细小的；动词：轻视、怠慢。它在 light 前多一个 s-。

entries.definition: noun: the ability to see, or something you see. It has no l, so it is sight, not slight or light.
entries.definitionCN: 视力；景象（名词）。它没有 l，所以是 sight，不是 slight 或 light。

entries.definition: noun: the dark part of the day. It starts with n- instead of l-, and is the opposite of day.
entries.definitionCN: 夜晚（名词）。它以 n- 开头而不是 l-，正是“白天”的反面。

entries.definition: noun: the bright flash in a storm. It is written without the e of lightening and has only two syllables.
entries.definitionCN: 闪电（名词）。拼写中没有 lightening 里的 e，只有两个音节。

entries.definition: the -ing form of lighten: making something lighter or brighter. It keeps the e and has three syllables; it is not lightning.
entries.definitionCN: lighten 的 -ing 形式：使变轻或变亮的过程。它保留 e，有三个音节；它不是“闪电”。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real, explainable links — real compounds and common phrases, not made-up rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实、可解释的联系——真实的复合词和常见短语，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: daylight = day + light: the light that belongs to the day.
normal.cn: daylight = day + light：属于白天的光，也就是日光。

normal.en: lighthouse = light + house: a house that holds a light to guide ships.
normal.cn: lighthouse = light + house：一座装着灯、用来指引船只的房子，也就是灯塔。

normal.en: lighten does two jobs: light (adj. not heavy) + -en = make less heavy; light (noun) + -en = make brighter.
normal.cn: lighten 有两个工作：light（形容词“轻”）+ -en = 使变轻；light（名词“光”）+ -en = 使变亮。

normal.en: lightning is the flash in a storm; lightening is the act of making something lighter or brighter. The e makes it the slow process, not the flash.
normal.cn: lightning 是暴风雨中的闪电；lightening 是使某物变轻或变亮的过程。多出的 e 表示这是一个过程，而不是那道闪光。

normal.en: shed light on something = make it clear. Light reveals what was hidden, and understanding is pictured as seeing.
normal.cn: shed light on something = 把某事讲清楚。光让隐藏的东西显露出来，而理解被想象成“看见”。

abstract.en: Light is a switch from hidden to seen. Symbol: ☾ → ☀ — a dark field becomes a lit field, and every shape in it appears.
abstract.cn: light 是从“隐藏”到“可见”的一次切换。符号：☾ → ☀——暗下来的场变成被照亮的场，里面每一个形状都显现出来。

abstract.en: The weight-light is a second switch: a load loses mass until it barely presses down. Same spelling, different origin — do not force one metaphor onto both.
abstract.cn: 表示“轻”的 light 是第二个开关：负担不断减少重量，直到几乎不再压下来。拼写相同，来源不同——不要把同一个比喻硬套到两者身上。

abstract.en: The extended senses follow visibility: what is lit can be seen, what is seen can be understood, and the angle of the light is the angle of the view.
abstract.cn: 引申义沿着“可见性”展开：被照亮的东西能被看见，被看见的东西能被理解，而光的角度就是看问题的角度。

examples.en: Turn off the light before you leave.
This jacket is very light, so it is good for summer.
examples.cn: 这件夹克很轻，所以适合夏天穿。

examples.en: The truth finally came to light.

dict_mnemonic.text: 来特（light）—— 光来得特别亮，是“光”；拎起来特别轻，是“轻” → light

groups.root: 两个同形异源的古英语词：lēoht“光”与 lēoht“轻”，分别来自印欧词根 *leuk- 和 *legwh-。

sensesIntro.en: Ten common senses of light. Two source words share one spelling: brightness removes darkness, while little weight removes pressure.
sensesIntro.cn: light 的十个常见义项。两个来源不同的词共用同一个拼写：明亮驱散黑暗，轻巧卸下压力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: darkness or weight is removed, so what was hidden or heavy becomes visible or easy.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗或重量被移走，原本被遮住或压住的东西变得可见、可承受。

branches.en: VISIBLE ENERGY: light itself, its source, setting it alight, and throwing it on a place.
branches.cn: 可见的能量：光本身、光的来源、把火点着、把光投向某处。

branches.en: COLOUR AND VIEW: how much light a colour seems to carry; which light you see an object in.
branches.cn: 颜色与视角：一种颜色看起来含多少光；你从哪束光里看一个对象。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE AS SIGHT: hidden facts enter the light and become known.
branches.cn: 知识即看见：隐藏的事实进入光中，就被人知道。

branches.en: WEIGHT REMOVED: a second, unrelated 'light' — little weight → little force → little seriousness.
branches.cn: 重量被移走：另一个来源无关的 light——重量小 → 力度小 → 严肃性小。

branches.en: HOMONYM NOTE: the left track belongs to the 'brightness' word; the right track belongs to the 'not heavy' word.
branches.cn: 同形异源提示：左边这条轨道属于“明亮”那个词；右边这条轨道属于“不重”那个词。

intro.en: Light is a highly productive root in two ways: it forms words about brightness and words about lightness of weight. Prefixes and suffixes send both cores into everyday vocabulary.
intro.cn: light 是一个高度能产的词根，有两条路：一条构成与“光”有关的词，一条构成与“轻”有关的词。前缀和后缀把这两个核心带进大量日常词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin lux / lūcis 'light' and lūmen 'light' are cognates of the brightness-light through PIE *leuk-. This family is not borrowed from the English word; it is a distant relative. Greek leukos 'white' belongs to the same root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lux / lūcis“光”和 lūmen“光”通过原始印欧语 *leuk- 与“明亮”义的 light 同源。这一族不是从英语这个词借出去的，而是远亲。希腊语 leukos“白”也属于同一词根。

items.meaning: to make or become less heavy
items.meaningCN: 使变轻；减轻（-en 表示“使……”，这里来自形容词“轻的”）
items.example: We lightened the load by leaving the tent behind.
items.exampleCN: 我们把帐篷留下，减轻了负担。

items.meaning: to make or become brighter
items.meaningCN: 使变亮；照亮（同形动词的另一支，来自名词“光”）
items.example: A few lamps lightened the dark room.
items.exampleCN: 几盏灯照亮了昏暗的房间。

items.meaning: gently; with little weight or force
items.meaningCN: 轻轻地；轻微地（-ly 是副词后缀）
items.example: She touched his shoulder lightly.
items.exampleCN: 她轻轻碰了碰他的肩膀。

items.meaning: to give someone knowledge or understanding
items.meaningCN: 启发；使明白（en- 表示“使进入”，lighten 表示“使变亮”）
items.example: The book enlightened me about the subject.
items.exampleCN: 这本书让我对这个主题有了新的认识。

items.meaning: the natural light of the day
items.meaningCN: 日光；白昼的光
items.example: We finished the work before daylight faded.
items.exampleCN: 我们在天色暗下来之前完成了工作。

items.meaning: the large lamp at the front of a vehicle
items.meaningCN: （汽车等的）前照灯；头灯
items.example: One headlight was broken.
items.exampleCN: 一个前照灯坏了。

items.meaning: weighing less than usual; also not serious or important
items.meaningCN: 轻量的；无足轻重的
items.example: She bought a lightweight jacket for the trip.
items.exampleCN: 她为这次旅行买了一件轻便夹克。

items.meaning: the arrangement or equipment that gives light
items.meaningCN: 照明；灯光设备（-ing 构成名词，表示行为或结果）
items.example: The stage lighting was too dim.
items.exampleCN: 舞台灯光太暗了。

items.meaning: a tower with a light that guides ships
items.meaningCN: 灯塔
items.example: The lighthouse stands at the end of the harbour.
items.exampleCN: 灯塔立在港口尽头。

latinEntries.meaning: clear and easy to understand
latinEntries.meaningCN: 清晰的；明白易懂的（luc- 表示“光”）

latinEntries.meaning: letting light pass through
giving off light
latinEntries.meaningCN: 发光的；明亮的（-ous 表示“充满……的”）

latinEntries.meaning: to light up; to make clear

groups.definition_en: to move quickly on foot, or to keep something operating
groups.scene: 叔叔开咖啡店，他说 My uncle runs a small coffee shop to make a living.
groups.sceneCN: 这里 run 是「经营」（第 3 个义项：让一件事持续运转）；句意：我叔叔经营一家小咖啡店谋生。

senses.title: Run: move fast on foot
senses.definition: to move quickly on foot, faster than walking
senses.definitionCN: 跑；奔跑
senses.example: She runs five kilometres every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上跑五公里。
senses.why: Core sense: the body moves continuously and quickly along a path. Every other sense keeps either the continuity or the directed motion.
senses.whyCN: 核心义：身体沿路径连续而快速地移动。其他义项都保留了“连续”或“有方向地动”这两个要素。

senses.title: Run: a machine operates
senses.definition: to operate or work, used about machines and engines
senses.definitionCN: （机器、发动机）运转；运行
senses.example: The engine was still running when we arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 我们到的时候发动机还在运转。
senses.why: A machine repeats the same internal motion without stopping. That repeated motion is the same 'continuous movement', moved inside the machine.
senses.whyCN: 机器不停重复内部运动；这种连续运动正是同一个“持续地动”，只是搬到了机器内部。

senses.title: Run: manage a business
senses.titleCN: 经营：让一件事持续运转
senses.definition: to manage or operate a business, organization, or system
senses.definitionCN: 经营；管理；运营
senses.example: My aunt runs a small bakery.
senses.exampleCN: 我姑姑经营一家小面包店。
senses.why: To run a business is to keep all its parts moving and working every day. Management is the act of preventing the machine from stopping.
senses.whyCN: 经营一门生意，就是让它所有部件每天持续运转。管理就是不让这台“机器”停下来的动作。

senses.title: Run: liquid flows
senses.definition: to flow, used about rivers, taps, and other liquids
senses.definitionCN: （液体）流动；流
senses.example: The river runs through the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河穿过老城。
senses.why: Old English rinnan meant both 'run' and 'flow'. Water moving along a channel has exactly the same continuous, directed motion as a runner.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 rinnan 同时表示“跑”和“流”。水沿水道前进，和奔跑者一样是连续、有方向的运动。

senses.title: Run: extend in a direction
senses.definition: to extend or continue in a particular direction
senses.definitionCN: 延伸；沿……走向
senses.example: The road runs along the coast for ten miles.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路沿海岸延伸十英里。
senses.why: A road does not move, but it presents a continuous line from one point to the next. The eye 'runs' along it, so the line is said to run.
senses.whyCN: 路不会动，但它从一点到另一点呈现出一条连续的线。眼睛沿着它“跑”，于是这条线也被说成 run。

senses.title: Run: last or continue
senses.titleCN: 持续：在时间中连续不断
senses.definition: to continue for a period of time or to have a particular length
senses.definitionCN: 持续；进行；有效
senses.example: The play ran for three months.
senses.exampleCN: 这部戏连续上演了三个月。
senses.why: Time is imagined as a path. Something that keeps going along that path 'runs' through time; its length is how far it runs.
senses.whyCN: 时间被想象成一条路径。持续存在的东西在这条路径上一直走，就是“跑”过时间；它的时长就是它跑了多远。

senses.title: Run for office: compete
senses.titleCN: 竞选：在争夺中跑在前面
senses.definition: to compete in an election for a political position
senses.definitionCN: （run for）竞选（公职）
senses.example: She is running for mayor this year.
senses.exampleCN: 她今年竞选市长。
senses.why: An election is a race. The candidate who 'runs' is the one moving toward the prize, and the campaign is the course.
senses.whyCN: 选举就是一场赛跑。参选者就是朝目标移动的人，竞选过程就是跑道。

senses.title: Run: colour spreads
senses.definition: to spread beyond the proper area, used about ink, dye, or colour
senses.definitionCN: （墨水、染料）洇开；掉色
senses.example: The red shirt ran in the wash and stained everything.
senses.exampleCN: 那件红衬衫洗的时候掉色，把所有东西都染了。
senses.why: Dye in water moves outward along the fabric without a fixed boundary. That uncontrolled spreading is still a kind of running — motion that escapes its channel.
senses.whyCN: 染料在水里沿着布料向外移动，没有固定边界。这种不受控的扩散仍是一种“跑”——跑出了原本的水道。

senses.title: Run: publish or print
senses.titleCN: 刊登：让内容进入发行流程
senses.definition: to print or publish something in a newspaper or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 刊登；发表
senses.example: The paper ran the story on its front page.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸把这篇报道登在了头版。
senses.why: A printing press runs through its cycle, and the copies run off the press. Publishing a story is letting it go through that run.
senses.whyCN: 印刷机跑完一轮流程，印本从机器上“跑”出来。刊登一篇报道，就是让它走完这一轮。

senses.title: A run: a continuous series
senses.definition: a continuous period or series of something
senses.definitionCN: （名词）一段连续的时间；一连串
senses.example: The team has had a long run of wins.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍已经连赢了很多场。
senses.why: The noun keeps the shape of a line: a run is one uninterrupted stretch of events, like one continuous run along a track.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了“一条线”的形状：a run 就是事件中一段不中断的连续，就像在跑道上一口气跑完的一段。

intro.en: Run is a merger of two related Old English verbs, one intransitive and one transitive. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: run 由两个相关的古英语动词合并而来，一个是不可及物的，一个是及物的。年代为大致估计。

items.en: rinnan, irnan (class III strong verb) meant 'to run, flow, run together', with past tense ran and past participle runnen. A second verb, ærnan / earnan, meant 'to ride, run to, reach, gain by running'.
items.cn: rinnan、irnan（第三类强动词）意为“跑、流动、汇流”，过去式 ran，过去分词 runnen。另一个动词 ærnan / earnan 意为“骑马、跑向、到达、靠奔跑获得”。

items.en: The modern verb merges the intransitive strong verb with the transitive weak causative. The r/n metathesis explains the variant forms rinnan and irnan; the initial letters sometimes switched places.
items.cn: 现代动词把不可及物的强动词和及物的弱使役动词合并在一起。r 与 n 的换位解释了 rinnan 和 irnan 这两种变体；开头的两个字母有时会互换位置。

items.en: The ancestor is *rinnaną 'to run, flow' (German rinnen 'to flow', rennen 'to run', Dutch rennen, Old Norse renna, Gothic rinnan). The causative is *rannjanan.
items.cn: 更早的祖词是原始日耳曼语 *rinnaną“跑、流动”（德语 rinnen“流”、rennen“跑”，荷兰语 rennen，古诺斯语 renna，哥特语 rinnan）。使役形式是 *rannjanan。

items.en: Watkins derives both verbs from PIE *rei- 'to run, flow', via a nasalized form *ri-ne-a-. Boutkan and others regard this as doubtful, because the supposed related forms are poorly attested, and list the word as having no certain Indo-European etymology.
items.cn: Watkins 把两个动词都追溯到原始印欧语 *rei-“跑、流动”，经由鼻音化形式 *ri-ne-a-。Boutkan 等人认为这一说法可疑，因为假定的同源形式证据不足，因此把该词列为“没有确定的印欧语词源”。

items.en: Latin currere 'to run' gave English current, cursor, course, occur and excursion. This family is not cognate with run; it is a separate word family with the same meaning, useful for comparison but not for etymology.
items.cn: 拉丁语 currere“跑”产生了英语 current、cursor、course、occur、excursion。这个词族与 run 并不同源，只是意思相同，可供比较，但不能当作 run 的词源。

items.en: The past tense is ran and the past participle is run (unchanged). The noun run is recorded from the 14th–15th centuries. The senses 'machine operates' (1560s), 'colour spreads' (1771), 'manage a business' (1861, American English) and 'publish' (1884) all developed later.
items.cn: 过去式是 ran，过去分词仍是 run（形式不变）。名词 run 在 14–15 世纪已有记录。“机器运转”（16 世纪 60 年代）、“颜色洇开”（1771）、“经营生意”（1861，美式英语）和“刊登”（1884）都是后来发展出来的义项。

note.en: Words below can be confused with run. The notes point to sound and spelling first, then meaning.
note.cn: 下面这些词容易和 run 混淆。说明先讲读音和拼写，再讲意思。

entries.definition: the past tense of run. The vowel is /æ/, not /ʌ/, so ran and run do not rhyme.
entries.definitionCN: run 的过去式。元音是 /æ/，不是 /ʌ/，所以 ran 和 run 并不押韵。

entries.definition: a very small brown bird. It has a silent w and a short /e/, so it sounds close to 'ren', not 'run'.
entries.definitionCN: 一种很小的棕色鸟（鹪鹩）。它的 w 不发音，元音是短 /e/，听起来接近“ren”，不是 run。

entries.definition: to destroy or spoil something; also the remains of a destroyed building. It has two syllables and a long /uː/.
entries.definitionCN: 毁坏；破坏；也可作名词，表示废墟。它有两个音节，元音是长音 /uː/。

entries.definition: past tense of run. It swaps u for a, so the spelling and the vowel both change.
entries.definitionCN: run 的过去式。它把 u 换成 a，拼写和元音都变了。

entries.definition: to destroy; a ruined building. It looks like run with an extra i, but has a long /uː/ and two syllables.
entries.definitionCN: 毁坏；废墟。它看起来像 run 多了一个 i，但读长音 /uː/，而且有两个音节。

entries.definition: the past participle of ring; also one step of a ladder. It ends in -ng, not -n.
entries.definitionCN: ring 的过去分词；也可指梯子的一级。它结尾是 -ng，不是 -n。

entries.definition: a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet. The final e is silent and the vowel is long /uː/.
entries.definitionCN: 古代日耳曼字母表中的一个字母（卢恩字母）。结尾的 e 不发音，元音是长音 /uː/。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real, explainable links — real suffixes, compounds and common phrases, not made-up rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实、可解释的联系——真实的后缀、复合词和常见短语，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: runner = run + -er: the person or thing that runs.
normal.cn: runner = run + -er：跑的人或跑的东西，也就是跑步者。

normal.en: runway = run + way: the strip of ground on which a plane runs to take off or land.
normal.cn: runway = run + way：飞机用来加速起飞或降落的那条地面，也就是跑道。

normal.en: running water = water that runs: a stream or tap water that keeps moving, not still water.
normal.cn: running water = 会流的水：不断流动的溪水或自来水，而不是静止的水。

normal.en: in the long run = over a long stretch of time, as if looking down a long track.
normal.cn: in the long run = 在很长一段路程之后，也就是从长远来看。

normal.en: run out of = the supply runs until nothing is left, like a runner reaching the end of the track.
normal.cn: run out of = 供应一直“跑”到没有为止，就像跑步者跑到跑道尽头。

abstract.en: Run is a line with an arrowhead and no full stop: →→→. It insists on continuing.
abstract.cn: run 是一条带箭头、没有句号的线：→→→。它坚持要继续下去。

abstract.en: The line can lie on the ground (a road), in water (a river), in time (a run of shows), or inside a machine (an engine running).
abstract.cn: 这条线可以铺在地上（路）、放在水里（河）、放进时间里（一连串演出），或者装进机器里（发动机运转）。

abstract.en: Management and publishing are the same line seen from the side: someone keeps the process moving. Run never means 'stay'; it always means 'keep going'.
abstract.cn: 经营和刊登是同一条线从侧面看的样子：有人让整个过程持续动起来。run 从不表示“停留”，它总是表示“继续走”。

examples.en: She runs to school every day.
He runs a small bookshop in the town centre.
examples.cn: 他在市中心经营一家小书店。

examples.en: We ran out of milk this morning.
examples.cn: 今天早上我们的牛奶用完了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 软（run）—— 跑到腿发软，还在继续跑 → run

groups.root: 源自古英语 rinnan / irnan，核心含义为“跑、流动”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten common senses of run. One image: continuous, directed motion — along the ground, through water, across time, or inside a working machine.
sensesIntro.cn: run 的十个常见义项。一个意象：连续、有方向的运动——沿地面、穿水流、跨时间，或在运转的机器内部。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: continuous, directed motion — something keeps moving along a path.
core.cn: 核心意象：连续、有方向的运动——某物沿一条路径不停向前。

branches.en: ALONG A PATH: feet, water and roads all trace a continuous line.
branches.cn: 沿路径：脚、水、道路都在描出一条连续的线。

branches.en: KEEPING IT MOVING: a machine runs by itself; a manager runs it on purpose.
branches.cn: 让它持续动：机器自己运转；管理者有意让它运转。

branches.en: LINE IN TIME: a play runs for months; a run is one continuous stretch.
branches.cn: 时间中的线：一部戏连续上演几个月；a run 就是一段不中断的连续。

branches.en: RACE AND ESCAPE: an election is a race; dye is motion that escapes its channel.
branches.cn: 竞赛与逃逸：选举是一场赛跑；染料是跑出水道的运动。

branches.en: THROUGH A PROCESS: a story goes through the press run and comes out printed.
branches.cn: 穿过流程：一篇报道走完印刷机的一轮运转，最后被印出来。

intro.en: Run is a productive verb root: suffixes and prefixes turn its 'continuous motion' into people, places, and processes.
intro.cn: run 是一个能产的动词词根：后缀和前缀把它“连续运动”的核心变成人、地点和过程。

items.meaning: a person or thing that runs
items.meaningCN: 跑步者；赛跑者（-er 表示做动作的人或物）
items.example: She is a fast runner.
items.exampleCN: 她跑得很快。

items.meaning: the activity of running; also continuing or in operation
items.meaningCN: 跑步；连续的；运转中的（-ing 表示动作或持续状态）
items.example: Running is good exercise.
items.exampleCN: 跑步是很好的锻炼。

items.meaning: someone who has escaped; out of control
items.meaningCN: 逃亡者；失控的（away 表示“离开”）
items.example: The runaway horse was finally caught.
items.exampleCN: 那匹脱缰的马终于被抓住了。

items.meaning: to run or show something again; a repeated broadcast
items.meaningCN: 重播；重新运行（re- 表示“再一次”）
items.example: The channel will rerun the series next month.
items.exampleCN: 这个频道下个月会重播这部剧。

items.meaning: to run faster than someone or something
items.meaningCN: 跑得比……快；超过（out- 表示“超过”）
items.example: No one can outrun him on this team.
items.exampleCN: 在这个队里没人跑得比他快。

items.meaning: to spread over and occupy something; to exceed a limit
items.meaningCN: 溢出；侵占；超出（over- 表示“越过、过量”）
items.example: The garden was overrun with weeds.
items.exampleCN: 花园里长满了杂草。

items.meaning: flowing or tending to flow, as a runny nose
items.meaningCN: 流动的；流鼻涕的（-y 构成形容词）
items.example: The child had a runny nose.
items.exampleCN: 那个孩子流鼻涕了。

items.meaning: the strip where aircraft take off and land; also a catwalk
items.meaningCN: 飞机跑道；（时装）T 台
items.example: The plane waited on the runway.
items.exampleCN: 飞机在跑道上等待。

items.meaning: a person or thing that came before and prepared the way
items.meaningCN: 先驱；前身（fore- 表示“在……之前”）
items.example: The telegram was a forerunner of the email.
items.exampleCN: 电报是电子邮件的先驱。

groups.definition_en: to get something into your hands or possession; to use up time or effort
groups.core_image: 拿到自己这里；花掉时间
groups.scene: 出门前提醒，你说 Don't forget to take an umbrella with you.
groups.sceneCN: 这里 take 是「带走、随身携带」（第 2 个义项）；句意：别忘了随身带把伞。

senses.title: Hand: reach out and grasp
senses.definition: to reach for something and hold it in your hand
senses.definitionCN: 伸手拿到某物并握在手里
senses.example: Take the keys from the table.
senses.exampleCN: 把桌上的钥匙拿起来。
senses.why: The core move is simple: the hand crosses the space to an object and closes on it. At this point nothing else has happened — no carrying, no using.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作很简单：手越过空间伸向物体，然后合拢握住。到这一步为止还没有别的事发生——没有带走，也没有使用。

senses.title: Carry: take it along
senses.definition: to carry something with you when you go somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 把某物带在身上去别处
senses.example: Take an umbrella with you; it may rain.
senses.exampleCN: 带把伞，可能会下雨。
senses.why: Once the hand has the object, the body moves and the object moves with it. Grasp becomes carry: the arrow keeps going away from the original place.
senses.whyCN: 手拿到东西之后，人一动，东西就跟着动。'抓住'于是变成'带走'——箭头从原来的位置继续向外延伸。

senses.title: Take a bus: be carried
senses.definition: to travel by using a bus, train, taxi, or similar vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 乘坐（公交、火车、出租车等）
senses.example: We took a taxi to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们坐出租车去了车站。
senses.why: Here the subject carries nothing; the vehicle carries the person. It is the same 'move away with' relation, with the roles swapped.
senses.whyCN: 这里主语并没有拿东西，而是交通工具把人带走。还是'带着走'的关系，只是角色反过来了。

senses.title: Receive: the thing comes to you
senses.definition: to accept something that is offered or given
senses.definitionCN: 接受别人给的东西或提议
senses.example: She took the job without hesitating.
senses.exampleCN: 她毫不犹豫地接受了这份工作。
senses.why: Take reverses direction here: instead of reaching out, you let what is offered cross into your boundary. Handing over is the mirror image of taking away.
senses.whyCN: take 在这里方向反过来：不是你伸手去够，而是让递过来的东西越过边界进入你这边。'递出'正是'拿走'的镜像动作。

senses.title: Take medicine: let it into the body
senses.definition: to swallow medicine, or to draw air or liquid into your body
senses.definitionCN: 服（药）；吸（气）
senses.example: Take this medicine twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 这药每天吃两次。
senses.why: The body is a container with an opening; what goes in is taken in. Physical grasp becomes ingestion — the object ends up inside you.
senses.whyCN: 身体是一个有开口的容器，从开口进去的东西就是被'拿进去'了。用手抓取变成了吞入，物体最终到了你身体里面。

senses.title: It takes an hour: use up time
senses.definition: to need a certain amount of time
senses.definitionCN: 需要、花费（若干时间）
senses.example: The trip takes about two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟行程大约要两个小时。
senses.why: Time is imagined as a measured supply you draw from. The action takes hours out of your day and they are gone — grasp becomes consumption of time.
senses.whyCN: 时间被想象成一份可以取用的量。这件事从你的一天里'拿走'几个小时，用完就没了——抓取于是变成了对时间的消耗。

senses.title: It takes courage: require a quality
senses.definition: to need a particular quality or amount of effort
senses.definitionCN: 需要（某种品质或努力）
senses.example: It takes courage to admit you were wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 承认自己错了需要勇气。
senses.why: This extends the time sense: a task draws on a resource — courage, patience, skill — and uses part of it up. Whatever a job consumes, the job 'takes'.
senses.whyCN: 这是时间义的延伸：一件事会从你身上取用某种资源——勇气、耐心、技巧——并消耗掉一部分。凡是任务要消耗的东西，都可以说它'需要'。

senses.title: Take it as a promise: interpret
senses.definition: to understand something in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式理解；把……看作
senses.example: I took her silence as a yes.
senses.exampleCN: 我把她的沉默当成了同意。
senses.why: Understanding is grasping with the mind: an idea outside you is picked up and brought inside. The hand's reach becomes the mind's reach.
senses.whyCN: 理解是用心智去抓取：外面的一条信息被接住，带进里面。手的伸展变成了心智的伸展。

senses.title: Take a photo: capture an image
senses.definition: to make a photograph, or to record an image or a measurement
senses.definitionCN: 拍照；记录（影像、数据）
senses.example: He took a photo of the sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 他拍了一张日落的照片。
senses.why: The camera grasps the light and fixes it, so the image is taken and kept. Capture is a technical kind of taking: the object is copied into your possession.
senses.whyCN: 相机'抓住'光线并把它固定下来，影像就被取走并留住了。'捕捉'是 take 的技术版：把对象复制一份收进自己的所有物里。

senses.title: Take five from ten: remove or subtract
senses.definition: to remove something, or to subtract one number from another
senses.definitionCN: 拿走；从……中减去
senses.example: Take five from ten and you get five.
senses.exampleCN: 十减去五等于五。
senses.why: This is the plainest reading of take away: the thing leaves its place and goes elsewhere. In arithmetic the number is simply taken out of the total.
senses.whyCN: 这是 take away 最字面的读法：东西离开原位、去了别处。在算术里，就是把一个数从总数里'拿走'。

intro.en: take is a Scandinavian loan that pushed out the native English verb for 'take'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: take 是一个斯堪的纳维亚借词，它把英语本土表示'拿'的动词挤出了常用位置。下面的年代为大致估计。

items.en: Old Norse taka meant 'to take, grasp, lay hold', with past tense tok and past participle tekinn. The same verb survives in Swedish ta and Danish tage.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 taka 意为'拿、抓、握住'，过去式 tok，过去分词 tekinn。同一个动词至今留在瑞典语 ta 和丹麦语 tage 里。

items.en: English borrowed it as tacan, first in northern texts where Scandinavian settlement was dense. From the 12th century the weaker sense 'get for oneself, obtain, receive' appears.
items.cn: 英语把它借进来作 tacan，最早出现在斯堪的纳维亚人聚居的北部文本中。到 12 世纪，较弱的'弄到自己手里、获得、收到'义开始出现。

items.en: The verb goes back to *takan- (root *tak- 'to take'), source also of Middle Low German tacken, Middle Dutch taken and Gothic tekan 'to touch'. The origin of the root itself is uncertain; OED suggests it may originally have meant 'to touch'.
items.cn: 这个词可追溯到原始日耳曼语 *takan-（词根 *tak- '拿'），中古低地德语 tacken、中古荷兰语 taken、哥特语 tekan'触摸'都来自这里。词根本身的来源不确定，OED 推测它最初也许是'触摸'的意思。

items.en: Latin had a semantic twin, capere 'to take, seize' (past participle captus), which gave English capture, accept, except and concept. It is a separate borrowing, not a cognate. Latin tangere 'to touch' looks similar to *tak-, but no proven link is established, so the resemblance should be treated as coincidence.
items.cn: 拉丁语有一个意思上的孪生词 capere'拿、抓'（过去分词 captus），它给英语留下了 capture、accept、except、concept。这是另一条借入路径，不是同源词。拉丁语 tangere'触摸'和 *tak- 看起来相似，但并没有被证实的亲缘关系，所以这种相似只应当作巧合。

items.en: Modern English keeps the strong pattern take – took – taken, and take replaced the older native verb niman, which died out around 1500 except in the slang sense 'steal'. The noun take 'that which is taken' dates from the 1650s.
items.cn: 现代英语保留强动词变化 take – took – taken；take 取代了更早的本土动词 niman，后者约在 1500 年消失，只剩'偷'这一俚语义。名词 take（'所取之物'）始见于 17 世纪 50 年代。

note.en: Words below are easy to mix up with take. The notes start with sound and spelling, then give the meaning.
note.cn: 下面这些词很容易和 take 混淆。说明先讲读音和拼写，再讲意思。

entries.definition: a short nail with a flat head; also a way of doing something. The vowel is short /æ/, not the diphthong /eɪ/.
entries.definitionCN: 图钉；方针、做法。元音是短音 /æ/，不是双元音 /eɪ/。

entries.definition: technology, or the technology industry. It also ends in /k/, but the vowel is /e/, not /eɪ/.
entries.definitionCN: 科技；科技行业。结尾同样是 /k/，但元音是 /e/，不是 /eɪ/。

entries.definition: a hard tropical wood used for furniture and boats. The long /iː/ makes it rhyme with peak, not with take.
entries.definitionCN: 柚木（一种做家具和船的硬木）。长音 /iː/ 让它与 peak 押韵，而不是与 take 押韵。

entries.definition: to create or cause something. Same -ake ending and same rhyme, but m- instead of t-, and the meaning is production.
entries.definitionCN: 制作；使成为。同样是 -ake 结尾、同样押韵，但开头是 m- 不是 t-，意思是'做'。

entries.definition: purpose or benefit, as in for the sake of. Same rhyme and ending; only the first letter differs.
entries.definitionCN: 缘故、利益，常用于 for the sake of。押韵和结尾相同，只差第一个字母。

entries.definition: a story. The first three letters and the vowel are the same, but it ends in -le, not -ke.
entries.definitionCN: 故事。前三个字母和元音相同，但结尾是 -le，不是 -ke。

entries.definition: a large container, or an armoured vehicle. Same ta- start, but the vowel is /æ/ and the ending is -nk.
entries.definitionCN: 大容器；坦克。开头同为 ta-，但元音是 /æ/，结尾是 -nk。

entries.definition: to speak. It starts with tal- and ends in -k, but the vowel is /ɔː/ and the l is pronounced.
entries.definitionCN: 说话。开头是 tal-、结尾是 -k，但元音是 /ɔː/，而且 l 要发音。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real phrases and real scenes. No invented etymology.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词、真实短语和真实场景，不编造词源。

normal.en: take a photo — here take means capture, not grab. The camera takes the image and keeps it, which is why we can also say capture a photo.
normal.cn: take a photo —— 这里的 take 是'捕捉'，不是'抓'。相机把影像取走并保存下来，所以也可以说 capture a photo。

normal.en: take medicine — the mouth is the boundary; the medicine crosses it and ends up inside the body.
normal.cn: take medicine —— 嘴就是那道边界；药越过它，最后进到身体里面。

normal.en: It takes an hour — time is treated as a supply you spend, so an activity draws hours out of your day.
normal.cn: It takes an hour —— 时间被视为一份可以花掉的存量，所以一件事会从你的一天里取走几个小时。

normal.en: take after someone — a family resemblance is 'taken' from your parents: a feature is received and carried with you.
normal.cn: take after someone —— 家族相似是从父母那里'拿'来的：某个特征被接收下来，一直带着。

normal.en: mistake = mis- (wrongly) + take. The word first meant 'misunderstand': to take something in the wrong way.
normal.cn: mistake = mis-（错误地）+ take。这个词最早就是'误解'的意思：把某物拿错了方向。

abstract.en: Abstractly, take is an arrow that ends at you: something outside your boundary crosses the line and becomes yours. Symbol: ○ ──▶ ●
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，take 是一支指向你的箭头：边界外的东西越过这条线，变成你的。符号：○ ──▶ ●

abstract.en: The same arrow can move an object (carry), a person (a bus takes you), or time (an hour is drawn out of your day). The geometry never changes; only the cargo does.
abstract.cn: 同一支箭头可以搬运物体（带走）、搬运人（公交车把你带走），也可以搬运时间（一小时从你的一天里被抽走）。几何形状从不改变，变的只是被搬的东西。

abstract.en: Mental taking repeats the move inward: an idea outside you is grasped and brought inside, which is why take can mean 'understand' and 'interpret'. Symbol: ○ ──▶ ● with the arrow ending in the mind.
abstract.cn: 心智上的 take 重复同一次向内移动：外面的一个想法被抓住、带进里面，所以 take 能表示'理解'和'解读'。符号：○ ──▶ ●，只是箭头终点落在心里。

examples.en: Take the umbrella with you; it looks like rain.
It took me an hour to finish the report.
examples.cn: 我花了一小时才写完报告。

examples.en: I took his advice and changed my plan.
examples.cn: 我接受了他的建议，改了计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 坦克（take）—— 坦克开过来，一把把东西都拿走了 → take

groups.root: 源自古诺斯语 taka（抓、拿），约 11 世纪借入英语，逐渐取代本土的 niman。

sensesIntro.en: Ten common senses of take. One movement runs through them all: reach out, close the hand, bring the thing to yourself.
sensesIntro.cn: take 的十个常见义项。一条动作贯穿全部：伸手、合掌、把东西带到自己这里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: reach out → grasp → bring the thing across the boundary to yourself.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸手 → 抓住 → 把东西越过边界带到自己这里。

branches.en: PHYSICAL TAKE: the hand reaches, closes, and the body carries the object away with it.
branches.cn: 物理拿取：手伸出去、合拢，然后身体把物体一起带走。

branches.en: BE CARRIED: the vehicle does the carrying and the person is the cargo — the same relation with the roles reversed.
branches.cn: 被载着走：交通工具承担'带'的动作，人成了被带的东西——同一种关系，角色对调。

branches.en: INTO ONE'S OWN: what is offered crosses in (accept), and what is understood crosses into the mind (interpret).
branches.cn: 进入自己的范围：递过来的东西越过边界（接受），被理解的东西进入心智（解读）。

branches.en: CONSUMPTION: body, time and effort are finite supplies; whatever a task draws out of them, the task 'takes'.
branches.cn: 消耗：身体、时间和精力都是有限存量；一件事从其中取走多少，它就'花费'多少。

branches.en: CAPTURE AND REMOVAL: an image is taken and kept; a number is taken out of the total.
branches.cn: 捕捉与移除：影像被取走并保存；数字从总数里被拿走。

intro.en: take is a highly productive element: prefixes and suffixes point its core motion — reach, grasp, remove — at new meanings.
intro.cn: take 是一个能产性很高的成分：前缀和后缀把它'伸手、抓住、拿走'的核心动作引导到新的含义上。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere 'to take, seize' (past participle captus) built a large English family with the forms cap-, cip- and cept-. This is a separate borrowing with the same core meaning, not a cognate of take.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capere'拿、抓'（过去分词 captus）在英语里造出了一个庞大的词族，形式包括 cap-、cip- 和 cept-。这是另一条借入路径，核心意思相同，但不是 take 的同源词。

items.meaning: to understand wrongly; an error
items.meaningCN: 误解；错误（mis- 表示'错误地'）
items.example: I mistook her umbrella for mine.
items.exampleCN: 我把她的伞错当成我的了。

items.meaning: to catch up with and pass someone or something
items.meaningCN: 追上并超过（over- 表示'越过、超过'）
items.example: The cyclist overtook the bus on the left.
items.exampleCN: 骑车的人从左侧超过了公交车。

items.structure: under- (upon oneself, beneath the load) + take
items.meaning: to take a task upon oneself; to begin work on it
items.meaningCN: 承担；着手做（under- 在这里表示'把担子放到自己身上'）
items.example: The company agreed to undertake the repairs.
items.exampleCN: 公司同意承担维修工作。

items.meaning: the amount taken in; also an opening where something enters
items.meaningCN: 摄入量；进气口（in- 表示'进入'）
items.example: You should cut down your salt intake.
items.exampleCN: 你该减少盐的摄入量。

items.meaning: the past participle: grasped, received, or occupied
items.meaningCN: 过去分词：被拿走的、被接受的、被占用的（-en 是过去分词词尾）
items.example: All the seats were taken.
items.exampleCN: 所有座位都被占了。

items.meaning: a person who takes something, often in a stated way
items.meaningCN: 取用者、接受者（-er 表示做这个动作的人）
items.example: She is a risk-taker by nature.
items.exampleCN: 她天生是个爱冒险的人。

items.meaning: the money a shop or business receives from sales
items.meaningCN: 营业收入（-ings 表示'收进来的东西'）
items.example: The shop's takings fell during the winter.
items.exampleCN: 这家店冬天的营业额下降了。

latinEntries.meaning: to catch and hold someone or something; the act of catching
to take something that is offered to you
latinEntries.meaningCN: 接受（把递来的东西拿过来）

latinEntries.meaning: to take one thing out of the rest; hence 'not including'
an idea the mind has taken in and gathered together
latinEntries.meaningCN: 概念（心智把信息收拢、拿住的结果）

groups.definition_en: to keep something in your hand or in place, so that it does not move or leave
groups.scene: 请人帮忙扶门，你说 Could you hold the door for a moment?
groups.sceneCN: 这里 hold 是「扶住、使保持在原位」（第 2 个义项）；句意：你能帮忙扶一会儿门吗？

senses.title: Grasp: keep in the hand
senses.definition: to have something in your hand and not let it go
senses.definitionCN: 把某物握在手里，不让它掉
senses.example: She held the cup with both hands.
senses.exampleCN: 她双手握着杯子。
senses.why: The hand closes into a ring around the object. That ring is a frame, and the frame is what stops the object from falling or leaving.
senses.whyCN: 手握成一个环，把物体圈在中间。这个环就是'框'，框住它，东西才不会掉、不会走。

senses.title: Hold the door: keep in position
senses.definition: to keep something in a particular position, especially so it does not fall or close
senses.definitionCN: 使某物保持在某个位置，尤指不让它倒下或关上
senses.example: Can you hold the door for me?
senses.exampleCN: 你能帮我扶住门吗？
senses.why: A door wants to swing shut; the hand takes over from the hinge and becomes the frame that fixes the position. Supporting is holding without grasping.
senses.whyCN: 门本来要自己关上；手代替了铰链，变成固定位置的'框'。'扶'是不用抓握的'握'。

senses.title: Contain: a bottle holds a litre
senses.definition: to have the capacity to contain something
senses.definitionCN: 有容纳某物的容量
senses.example: This bottle holds one litre of water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个瓶子能装一升水。
senses.why: A container is a frame made of walls. What is inside is kept inside, so hold moves from the hand to the vessel, and then to the idea of capacity.
senses.whyCN: 容器是用壁做成的'框'，里面的东西被留在里面。于是 hold 从手转到容器，再转指容量。

senses.title: Hold back: restrain
senses.definition: to stop someone or something from moving forward, or to control a feeling
senses.definitionCN: 阻止某人或某物前进；抑制（情绪）
senses.example: The barrier held the crowd back.
senses.exampleCN: 护栏把人群挡在了后面。
senses.why: Here the frame pushes outward instead of enclosing: force is applied against movement. Holding back tears puts the same frame around a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这里的'框'不是围住，而是向外推：力逆着运动方向使。'忍住眼泪'就是把同一个框套在情绪上。

senses.title: Hold someone: detain
senses.definition: to keep someone in custody or make them stay
senses.definitionCN: 拘留；使某人不能离开
senses.example: The police held him for questioning.
senses.exampleCN: 警方把他扣留讯问。
senses.why: A cell is a legal frame; the person is kept inside it. Custody is containment applied to a human being.
senses.whyCN: 牢房是法律意义上的'框'，人被留在框里。'拘留'就是把'容纳'用在人身上。

senses.title: Hold a ticket: keep possession
senses.definition: to have and keep something as yours
senses.definitionCN: 持有、保留（属于自己的东西）
senses.example: Hold on to your ticket until the end of the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 车票留到行程结束再扔。
senses.why: The hand keeps the object from leaving your possession. Holding is the state version of taking: what was taken stays taken.
senses.whyCN: 手让东西不离开你的所有范围。'持有'是 take 的状态版：拿到的东西继续留在手里。

senses.title: Hold office: occupy a position
senses.definition: to have a job, a position, or a record
senses.definitionCN: 担任（职务）；保持（纪录）
senses.example: She holds the world record in swimming.
senses.exampleCN: 她保持着游泳世界纪录。
senses.why: A position is imagined as a place; holding it means your grip keeps you in that place. Possession becomes occupation.
senses.whyCN: 职位被想象成一个位置；'握'住它就等于让自己留在这个位置上。'拥有'于是变成'占据'。

senses.title: Hold a meeting: carry on
senses.definition: to organize and carry on an event such as a meeting or ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 举行、进行（会议、仪式等活动）
senses.example: We hold a team meeting every Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 我们每周一开团队会。
senses.why: This comes from the older sense 'maintain, carry on': the event is kept in existence for its duration. The frame here is made of time.
senses.whyCN: 这来自更早的'维持、进行'义：活动在被'保持存在'的这段时间里持续进行。这里的'框'是时间做成的。

senses.title: Hold an opinion: believe
senses.definition: to have a belief or opinion
senses.definitionCN: 持有（观点、信念）
senses.example: He holds strong views about education.
senses.exampleCN: 他对教育有很坚定的看法。
senses.why: An idea is grasped mentally and not released: you keep it in mind, so you 'hold' it. Mental holding mirrors manual holding.
senses.whyCN: 一个想法被心智抓住、不放掉：你把它留在心里，所以说你'持有'它。心智的握，是手的握的镜像。

senses.title: The rule still holds: remain valid
senses.definition: to remain true or valid
senses.definitionCN: 仍然成立、有效
senses.example: That argument no longer holds.
senses.exampleCN: 那个论点已经站不住了。
senses.why: An argument or rule is a structure that must keep its shape under pressure. If it neither breaks nor slips, it holds — validity is stability.
senses.whyCN: 论点或规则是一个要在压力下保持形状的结构。如果它没断、没滑，它就'握得住'——'有效'就是稳定。

intro.en: hold is a native English strong verb with a Germanic family behind it. Its oldest recorded sense was probably not 'grasp' but 'tend, watch over'.
intro.cn: hold 是英语本族语的强动词，背后是一整个日耳曼词族。它最早被记录的义项也许不是'握'，而是'照料、看守'。

items.en: West Saxon healdan, Anglian haldan, meant 'to contain, grasp, retain; to observe or fulfil a custom; to possess, control, rule; to detain; to foster, cherish, keep watch over'. It was a class VII strong verb: past tense heold, past participle healden.
items.cn: 西撒克逊方言作 healdan，盎格利亚方言作 haldan，意为'容纳、握住、保留；遵守并履行习俗；拥有、控制、统治；扣留；养育、珍视、看守'。它是第七类强动词：过去式 heold，过去分词 healden。

items.en: The ancestor is *haldanan, shared with Old Saxon haldan, Old Frisian halda, Old Norse halda, Dutch houden, German halten and Gothic haldan 'to tend'.
items.cn: 祖词是原始日耳曼语 *haldanan，古撒克逊语 haldan、古弗里斯语 halda、古诺斯语 halda、荷兰语 houden、德语 halten 和哥特语 haldan'照料'都同出一源。

items.en: On the evidence of Gothic and a secondary Old English sense, OED calls it 'generally accepted' that the verb first meant 'to keep, tend, watch over' — as with grazing cattle — and only later widened to 'have as one's own'. The sense of looking survives in behold.
items.cn: 根据哥特语和古英语中的一个次要义项，OED 认为'普遍接受'的看法是：这个动词最初意为'看守、照料、看护'——比如看牛吃草——后来才扩展为'归自己所有'。'看'这一层意思还留在 behold 里。

items.en: Latin tenere 'to hold' (stem ten-/tain-) built a parallel family: contain, retain, maintain, detain, tenant. It is a separate borrowing, not a cognate. The old past participle holden was replaced by held in the 16th century but survives in beholden and in some legal wording.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tenere'握住'（词干 ten-/tain-）另造出了一族词：contain、retain、maintain、detain、tenant。这是另一条借入路径，不是同源词。旧的过去分词 holden 在 16 世纪被 held 取代，但仍活在 beholden 和某些法律用语里。

items.en: Modern English has hold – held – held. The noun hold is older than it looks: c. 1100 'act of holding', c. 1200 'a grip or support', and from the 1950s 'a waiting state' in telephony. The ship's hold is a different word, a 15th-century alteration of holl 'hull, hollow place'.
items.cn: 现代英语的变化是 hold – held – held。名词 hold 比看上去更古老：约 1100 年指'握的行为'，约 1200 年指'可抓握的支撑物'，20 世纪 50 年代起又指电话中的'等待接通状态'。船舱的 hold 是另一个词，是 15 世纪对 holl（'船壳、空腔'）的改写。

note.en: Words below can be confused with hold. Sound and spelling come first, meaning second.
note.cn: 下面这些词容易和 hold 混淆。先讲读音和拼写，再讲意思。

entries.definition: the past tense of hole, meaning 'made a hole in' or 'hit a ball into a hole'. It sounds exactly like hold; only the -ed tells them apart on paper.
entries.definitionCN: hole（打洞；把球打进洞）的过去式。读音和 hold 完全相同，纸面上只能靠 -ed 分辨。

entries.definition: an opening or a hollow space. It lacks the final /d/, so the tongue stops earlier.
entries.definitionCN: 洞；孔。少了结尾的 /d/，舌头停得更早。

entries.definition: brave, or strong and clear in appearance. Same -old ending, but b- instead of h-.
entries.definitionCN: 大胆的；醒目的。同样是 -old 结尾，但开头是 b- 不是 h-。

entries.definition: the past tense of tell. Same rhyme and ending; the meaning is speaking, not holding.
entries.definitionCN: tell 的过去式。押韵、结尾相同，但意思是'告诉'，不是'握住'。

entries.definition: This is hold's own past tense and past participle, not another word. It looks like hold but has a short /e/ and no o.
entries.definitionCN: 这就是 hold 自己的过去式和过去分词，不是另一个词。它长得像 hold，但元音是短音 /e/，而且没有 o。

entries.definition: having lived a long time. It is hold with the h removed, and the meaning is age, not grip.
entries.definitionCN: 年老的；旧的。就是去掉 h 的 hold，意思是年龄，不是握。

entries.definition: a yellow precious metal. Same -old ending, but starts with g- and is a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 黄金。同样是 -old 结尾，但开头是 g-，而且是名词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real phrases, each explaining one part of hold.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词和真实短语，每一个都解释 hold 的某一面。

normal.en: hold the door — your hand is the frame that keeps the door in place, replacing the hinge for a moment.
normal.cn: hold the door —— 你的手就是让门留在原位的'框'，暂时替代了铰链。

normal.en: hold a meeting — from the older sense 'carry on, maintain': the meeting is kept in existence for its length.
normal.cn: hold a meeting —— 来自更早的'进行、维持'义：会议被'保持存在'一段时间。

normal.en: hold water — an argument that holds water keeps its shape under testing, so it remains valid.
normal.cn: hold water —— 站得住脚的论点在检验下能保持形状，所以它是有效的。

normal.en: withhold = with (away, back) + hold. To withhold is to hold something back from the person who should get it.
normal.cn: withhold = with（离开、往回）+ hold。'扣留'就是把本该给别人的东西握回去、不给出去。

normal.en: household = house + hold, where hold had a Middle English sense 'dwelling, habitation' — the people and things of one dwelling.
normal.cn: household = house + hold，这里的 hold 在中古英语里有'住所、居所'的意思，即同一处住所里的人与物。

abstract.en: Abstractly, hold is a frame drawn around a thing: the frame stops the thing from leaving. No force is needed; what matters is staying. Symbol: [ ● ]
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，hold 是在东西周围画出的一个'框'：框让东西离不开。它不需要用力，关键是'留住'。符号：[ ● ]

abstract.en: The frame can be made of different materials — a hand, a wall, a law, a stare. That is why one verb covers grip, containment, custody and attention. Symbol: [ ● ] with thicker walls.
abstract.cn: 这个框可以用不同材料做成——一只手、一堵墙、一条法律、一道目光。所以同一个动词能覆盖握、容纳、扣留和注视。符号：[ ● ]，只是框壁更厚。

abstract.en: The frame can also be turned inward: what you hold in mind is what you refuse to release — an opinion, a secret, a memory. Symbol: [ ● ] where the dot is an idea.
abstract.cn: 这个框也可以向内转：你在心里'握'住的东西，就是你拒绝放手的——一个观点、一个秘密、一段记忆。符号：[ ● ]，只是框里的点变成了想法。

examples.en: Can you hold the door for me?
This jug holds two litres of milk.
examples.cn: 这个罐子能装两升牛奶。

examples.en: She held the umbrella against the wind.

dict_mnemonic.text: 厚的手掌（hold）—— 手掌够厚，才握得住、托得稳 → hold

groups.root: 源自古英语 healdan（握住、看守），与德语 halten 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Ten common senses of hold. All of them use one shape: something is put inside a frame and kept from leaving.
sensesIntro.cn: hold 的十个常见义项。它们都共用同一个形状：把东西放进一个框里，让它离不开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frame — hand, wall, law, attention — around a thing, so it stays where it is.
core.cn: 核心意象：用手、墙、法律或注意力，在东西周围围出一个'框'，让它留在原处。

branches.en: PHYSICAL: the hand grasps or supports, and the frame fixes a position.
branches.cn: 物理层面：手握或托，框把位置固定住。

branches.en: ENCLOSURE: a vessel holds volume, a cell holds a person — capacity and custody are the same frame.
branches.cn: 围合：容器握住容积，牢房握住人——容量和扣留是同一个框。
